bundles.name: valid-the-current-key
bundles.about: The operator's fingerprint equals the computed fingerprint of an entry: that key is pinned.

bundles.name: valid-a-retired-key
bundles.about: A retired key can be pinned; the statements in an offer lead the host to the current one.

bundles.name: absent-fingerprint
bundles.about: No entry has the operator's fingerprint: nothing is pinned.

bundles.name: valid-unknown-members-are-ignored
bundles.about: Members setup does not know, such as a custody label a server should not send, change nothing.

bundles.name: refused-fingerprint-member-disagrees-with-its-key
bundles.about: The entry claims the operator's fingerprint but holds another key: a match on the member would pin the wrong key.

bundles.name: refused-fingerprint-member-disagrees-in-another-entry
bundles.about: One entry is right and matches, another disagrees with its key: the whole bundle is malformed.

bundles.name: refused-fingerprint-member-absent
bundles.about: An entry without its fingerprint member is malformed: the server always writes it, and a bundle that leaves it out is not one this contract describes.

bundles.name: refused-fingerprint-member-in-uppercase
bundles.about: The fingerprint member is lowercase hexadecimal.

bundles.name: refused-small-order-key
bundles.about: An entry whose key is a point of small order is refused, even though its fingerprint member is right.

bundles.name: refused-malformed-key-line
bundles.about: An entry whose public_key is not a key line.

bundles.name: refused-unknown-state
bundles.about: A state is current or retired.

bundles.name: refused-keys-missing
bundles.about: A bundle without keys is malformed.

cases.name: valid-single-signature
cases.about: One signature by the pinned key. The signer's floor becomes the counter.

cases.name: valid-trailing-line-feed
cases.about: One final line feed after the object is allowed.

cases.name: valid-signature-covers-the-line-feed
cases.about: The signature covers every delivered byte, the final line feed included.

cases.name: valid-double-signature-both-pinned
cases.about: Two entries, both keys pinned: the first verifying entry is the signer and both floors advance.

cases.name: valid-entry-for-unpinned-key-is-ignored
cases.about: An entry for a key the host does not pin is ignored, even when it comes first and its signature is wrong.

cases.name: valid-four-signature-entries
cases.about: The most entries a signature file may hold; only the pinned key's entry counts.

cases.name: valid-other-keys-floor-is-dropped
cases.about: A floor kept for a key the host no longer pins does not survive.

cases.name: valid-counter-one-above-the-floor
cases.about: A counter one above the signer's floor, the highest counter attempted, is new.

cases.name: valid-counter-at-the-largest-safe-integer
cases.about: 2^53-1 is the largest counter.

cases.name: valid-minimum-version-satisfied
cases.about: min_from equal to the running version is satisfied.

cases.name: valid-no-minimum-version
cases.about: min_from is optional.

cases.name: valid-version-numbers-compare-as-numbers
cases.about: 0.1.10 is newer than 0.1.9 although it sorts before it as text.

cases.name: valid-nine-digit-version-numbers
cases.about: Each version number may have nine digits.

cases.name: valid-track-minor
cases.about: The minor track takes a newer minor version of the same major.

cases.name: valid-minor-track-newer-patch
cases.about: The minor track takes a newer patch too.

cases.name: valid-windows-artifact-name
cases.about: The windows file name ends in .exe.

cases.name: valid-all-six-platforms
cases.about: Every platform may appear once.

cases.name: valid-size-of-128-mib
cases.about: 128 MiB is the largest artifact.

cases.name: valid-size-of-one-byte
cases.about: One byte is the smallest artifact.

cases.name: valid-validity-of-400-days
cases.about: 400 days between issued_at and expires_at is the longest validity.

cases.name: valid-one-second-before-expiry
cases.about: A release is usable until its expires_at.

cases.name: valid-issued-24-hours-ahead-of-the-clock
cases.about: A host takes a release issued up to 24 hours after its own clock.

cases.name: valid-first-second-of-1970
cases.about: Instants start at 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z.

cases.name: valid-leap-day
cases.about: February 29 of a leap year is a date.

cases.name: valid-manifest-of-exactly-16-kib
cases.about: 16,384 bytes is the longest manifest; spaces between tokens are allowed.

cases.name: valid-members-in-another-order
cases.about: A manifest lists its members, and each artifact its own, in any order: here the opposite of the order the contract shows.

cases.name: valid-spaces-between-every-token
cases.about: A space may stand on each side of every brace, bracket, colon and comma that is not inside a string.

cases.name: valid-another-order-spaces-and-a-final-line-feed
cases.about: The three together: opposite order, spaces between every token and one final line feed.

cases.name: valid-rollover-to-a-successor
cases.about: The host pins the old key; the release is signed by its successor. The floor moves to the successor.

cases.name: valid-chain-of-two-rollovers
cases.about: Statements are followed in the order given.

cases.name: valid-chain-of-eight-rollovers
cases.about: Eight statements is the longest chain.

cases.name: valid-rollover-for-a-key-that-is-not-pinned-is-ignored
cases.about: A statement from a key the host does not pin changes nothing; the release is signed by the pinned key.

cases.name: valid-identical-statement-twice
cases.about: The same statement twice is not a conflict: the first is followed and the second, from a key no longer pinned, is ignored.

cases.name: valid-two-statements-naming-the-same-successor
cases.about: Two statements that differ only in their time name one successor: no fork.

cases.name: valid-statements-from-a-replaced-key-are-ignored
cases.about: The host already followed team to team-next; later statements from team, even naming another key, are ignored.

cases.name: valid-rollover-to-a-key-already-pinned
cases.about: The replaced key leaves the set; the successor was already in it.

cases.name: valid-pinned-successor-keeps-the-higher-floor-it-had
cases.about: The host pins team and team-next and follows team to team-next. The successor's own floor, 9, is higher than the replaced key's, 3, and stays 9.

cases.name: valid-pinned-successor-takes-the-higher-floor-of-the-replaced-key
cases.about: The replaced key's floor, 9, is higher than the successor's own, 3: the successor holds 9.

cases.name: valid-successor-that-inherits-no-floor-has-none-after
cases.about: Neither team nor its successor has attempted anything: the successor holds no floor, and a floor of 0 is not listed.

cases.name: valid-floor-of-zero-is-not-listed
cases.about: A pinned key whose floor is 0, nothing attempted, has no floor after the release; the signer's is the counter.

cases.name: valid-statement-members-in-another-order
cases.about: A rollover statement lists its members in any order.

cases.name: valid-statement-spaces-between-every-token
cases.about: A space may stand between any two tokens of a statement.

cases.name: valid-statement-with-a-final-line-feed
cases.about: One final line feed may end a statement; the signature covers it, as it covers every delivered byte.

cases.name: refused-rollover-from-an-unpinned-key
cases.about: The release is signed by the successor in a statement the host cannot accept.

cases.name: refused-rollovers-out-of-order
cases.about: A statement whose from key is not yet pinned when its turn comes is ignored.

cases.name: refused-rollover-with-a-wrong-signature
cases.about: The statement is signed by another key than its from key.

cases.name: refused-rollover-signed-by-another-pinned-key
cases.about: team's statement is signed by project, which the host pins too. The signature verifies under project and not under team, the key the statement says it replaces, so the statement is ignored and the release signed by the successor finds no pinned key.

cases.name: refused-rollover-from-the-second-pin-signed-by-the-first
cases.about: project's statement is signed by team, which the host pins too: a statement is judged by the key it names as from, whichever pinned key signed it.

cases.name: refused-rollover-signed-by-its-own-successor
cases.about: The new key vouches for itself: the statement is signed by team-next, not by team, so it is ignored.

cases.name: refused-rollover-with-the-release-prefix
cases.about: A statement signed over the release prefix is not a statement.

cases.name: refused-rollover-without-the-prefix
cases.about: A statement signed over its bytes alone is not a statement.

cases.name: refused-rollover-statement-with-another-schema
cases.about: The statement's schema must be exact.

cases.name: refused-rollover-to-a-malformed-key-line
cases.about: The to member must be a valid public key line.

cases.name: refused-rollover-from-uppercase-fingerprint
cases.about: The from member is lowercase hexadecimal.

cases.name: refused-rollover-to-itself
cases.about: A statement that replaces a key with itself is not a statement.

cases.name: refused-rollover-statement-as-an-array
cases.about: A statement is one object. The four values in an array are not a statement, though they are in the order of its members.

cases.name: refused-rollover-statement-member-name-in-another-case
cases.about: Member names are matched exactly: From is not from, so from is missing and From is an unknown member.

cases.name: refused-rollover-with-a-bad-envelope
cases.about: The statement's base64 holds no whitespace.

cases.name: refused-rollover-to-a-small-order-key
cases.about: The to key is the identity point, which accepts a universal signature. The statement is ignored, so the release it would have vouched for finds no pinned key.

cases.name: refused-two-statements-naming-different-successors
cases.about: Two statements from one pinned key naming different successors: someone else holds the key. The host reports both successors.

cases.name: refused-conflict-in-the-other-order
cases.about: The order of the two statements does not matter.

cases.name: refused-conflict-even-when-the-release-is-signed-by-the-pinned-key
cases.about: The conflict is evidence against the key, whoever signed the release.

cases.name: refused-conflict-reports-the-first-two-successors
cases.about: With three successors the host reports the first statement's and the first that differs from it.

cases.name: refused-conflict-deeper-in-the-chain
cases.about: A key that joined the pins through the chain can fork too.

cases.name: refused-a-fork-signed-by-the-wrong-key-is-no-fork
cases.about: The second statement's signature is not the from key's, so it is ignored: the first is followed, and the release signed by the thief's key finds no pinned key.

cases.name: refused-nine-rollovers
cases.about: An offer carries at most eight statements.

cases.name: refused-key-not-pinned
cases.about: The only entry names a key the host does not pin.

cases.name: refused-no-pinned-keys
cases.about: A host with no pins accepts nothing.

cases.name: refused-entry-for-an-unknown-fingerprint
cases.about: A fingerprint that names no known key is just an unpinned key.

cases.name: refused-successor-signature-without-a-statement
cases.about: A release signed by the successor needs the statement that replaces the pinned key.

cases.name: refused-flipped-manifest-byte
cases.about: One byte of the manifest changed after signing.

cases.name: refused-flipped-signature-byte
cases.about: One bit of the signature changed.

cases.name: refused-signature-without-the-prefix
cases.about: The signature covers the manifest alone, without the prefix.

cases.name: refused-prefix-of-the-rollover-statement
cases.about: The signature covers the manifest under the rollover prefix.

cases.name: refused-prefix-without-its-line-feed
cases.about: The prefix ends in a line feed.

cases.name: refused-prefix-of-another-version
cases.about: A v2 prefix is another message.

cases.name: refused-entry-claims-the-pinned-key-with-another-keys-signature
cases.about: The entry names the pinned key; the signature is by another. The key field only selects which pinned key to try.

cases.name: refused-only-the-unverifying-entry-is-pinned
cases.about: The pinned key's entry is wrong; a valid entry for an unpinned key does not help.

cases.name: refused-signature-with-s-not-below-the-group-order
cases.about: S plus the group order is the same point and another encoding; a verifier refuses it (RFC 8032, 5.1.7).

cases.name: refused-signature-whose-r-is-the-identity-point
cases.about: R is the identity point and S is made from the key's own scalar, so the verification equation holds; a host refuses a small-order R.

cases.name: refused-platform-missing
cases.about: The release has no build for this host.

cases.name: refused-expired
cases.about: The host's clock is past expires_at.

cases.name: refused-at-the-moment-of-expiry
cases.about: A release is expired at expires_at itself.

cases.name: refused-issued-more-than-24-hours-ahead-of-the-clock
cases.about: A release issued 25 hours after the host's clock is refused as invalid, the direction the signed envelope already guards.

cases.name: refused-issued-one-second-over-24-hours-ahead
cases.about: 24 hours and one second ahead is refused; exactly 24 hours is not.

cases.name: refused-counter-at-the-attempted-floor
cases.about: A counter equal to the signer's floor, the highest counter attempted, was attempted already.

cases.name: refused-counter-below-the-floor
cases.about: A counter below the floor is an old release.

cases.name: refused-release-already-tried
cases.about: The counter is at the floor and the host's last result names this manifest as rolled back.

cases.name: refused-rolled-back-release-after-a-newer-attempt
cases.about: The floor moved on; the last result still names this manifest as rolled back.

cases.name: refused-counter-at-the-floor-after-a-commit
cases.about: The last result names this manifest, but it was committed, not rolled back.

cases.name: refused-counter-at-the-floor-another-release-rolled-back
cases.about: The last result names another manifest.

cases.name: valid-last-result-names-this-manifest-but-the-counter-is-new
cases.about: The floor decides, not the last result: a counter above it is new.

cases.name: refused-floor-carried-over-a-rollover
cases.about: The old key's floor guards its successor.

cases.name: refused-when-one-of-two-signers-has-attempted-it
cases.about: Every verifying pinned signer must find the counter new.

cases.name: refused-when-the-first-signer-in-the-file-has-attempted-it
cases.about: project signs first and its floor is the counter; team's is below it. Every verifying pinned signer is checked.

cases.name: refused-when-the-second-signer-in-the-file-has-attempted-it
cases.about: project signs first and its floor is below the counter; the second signer, team, has attempted it. Checking only the first signer would take this release.

cases.name: valid-the-floor-of-a-pinned-key-whose-signature-fails-is-not-checked
cases.about: project's entry does not verify, so project is not a signer: its floor, 9, does not refuse the release, and it keeps that floor. team signs.

cases.name: refused-pinned-successor-keeps-the-floor-it-had
cases.about: The host pins team and team-next and follows team to team-next, which signs the release. The successor's own floor, 9, is above the counter although the replaced key's, 3, is not.

cases.name: refused-pinned-successor-takes-the-floor-of-the-replaced-key
cases.about: The replaced key's floor, 9, is above the counter and the successor's own, 3, is not: the successor holds 9.

cases.name: refused-same-version-as-running
cases.about: The release is the running version.

cases.name: refused-older-patch
cases.about: The running version is newer.

cases.name: refused-older-minor
cases.about: The running version is newer. The release is also off the patch track; the version check comes first.

cases.name: refused-older-major
cases.about: The running version is newer.

cases.name: refused-version-numbers-compare-as-numbers
cases.about: 0.1.9 is older than 0.1.10 although it sorts after it as text.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-a-pre-release-suffix
cases.about: 0.1.0-dev, the version of a development build, has a suffix. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-build-metadata
cases.about: 0.1.0+5 carries build metadata. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-a-leading-v
cases.about: v0.1.0 is a tag, not a version. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-that-is-empty
cases.about: An empty string is not a version. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-that-is-a-word
cases.about: dev is not a version. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-two-numbers
cases.about: 0.1 has two numbers. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-four-numbers
cases.about: 0.1.0.0 has four numbers. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-an-empty-number
cases.about: 0.1. has no patch number. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-a-leading-zero
cases.about: 0.01.0 writes the number 1 with a leading zero. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-a-plus-sign
cases.about: 0.1.+0 puts a sign on a number, which a function that parses integers takes. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-a-minus-sign
cases.about: 0.1.-0 puts a sign on a number, which a function that parses integers takes. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-a-letter-after-a-number
cases.about: 0.1.0a: a reader that stops at the first character that is not a digit takes 0.1.0. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-a-letter-for-a-number
cases.about: 0.1.x has no patch number. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-a-leading-space
cases.about: A space before 0.1.0 is not trimmed. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-a-trailing-space
cases.about: A space after 0.1.0 is not trimmed. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-a-trailing-line-feed
cases.about: A line feed after 0.1.0 is not trimmed. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-digits-that-are-not-ascii
cases.about: The numbers are written with the full-width digits 0, 1 and 0. It cannot be compared with the release's, so it is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-running-version-with-a-ten-digit-number
cases.about: A version number has at most nine digits, so 0.0.1000000000 cannot be compared with the release's and is refused as a downgrade.

cases.name: refused-patch-track-newer-minor
cases.about: The patch track keeps the running major and minor.

cases.name: refused-patch-track-newer-major
cases.about: The patch track keeps the running major and minor.

cases.name: refused-minor-track-newer-major
cases.about: The minor track keeps the running major: a major jump is never remote.

cases.name: refused-running-version-below-the-minimum
cases.about: min_from is newer than the running version.

cases.name: refused-other-architecture
cases.about: The release has no linux/arm64 build.

cases.name: refused-other-operating-system
cases.about: The release has no darwin/amd64 build.

cases.name: refused-newer-service-definition
cases.about: The release needs a service definition newer than the host's.

cases.name: valid-service-definition-the-host-has
cases.about: The host's definition is as new as the release needs.

cases.name: valid-a-host-with-a-newer-service-definition
cases.about: The host's definition, 2, is ahead of the 1 the release needs: a release is refused only when its definition is newer than the host's.

cases.name: refused-service-definition-at-the-largest-safe-integer
cases.about: 2^53-1 is the largest service definition a manifest may need: the manifest is valid, and the host's 1 is older.

cases.name: order-signature-before-manifest
cases.about: A flipped manifest that is also invalid: the signature is judged first.

cases.name: order-pins-before-manifest
cases.about: An unpinned signer and an invalid manifest: the pins are judged first.

cases.name: order-signature-file-before-conflict
cases.about: A malformed signature file and conflicting statements: the file is judged first.

cases.name: order-conflict-before-pins
cases.about: Conflicting statements and an unpinned signer: the conflict is judged first.

cases.name: order-manifest-before-expiry
cases.about: An invalid and expired manifest: validity is judged first.

cases.name: order-expiry-before-platform
cases.about: An expired release without this platform: the clock is judged first.

cases.name: order-platform-before-counter
cases.about: A replayed counter for another platform: the platform is judged first.

cases.name: order-counter-before-version
cases.about: A replayed counter and an older version: the counter is judged first.

cases.name: order-track-before-minimum
cases.about: Off track and below the minimum: the track is judged first.

cases.name: order-minimum-before-service-definition
cases.about: Below the minimum and an outdated service definition: the minimum is judged first.

cases.name: order-signature-before-an-unreadable-running-version
cases.about: A signature that does not cover the manifest and an unreadable running version: the signature is judged first.

cases.name: order-platform-before-an-unreadable-running-version
cases.about: A release without this platform and an unreadable running version: the platform is judged first.

cases.name: order-counter-before-an-unreadable-running-version
cases.about: A replayed counter and an unreadable running version: the counter is judged first.

cases.name: order-an-unreadable-running-version-before-the-track
cases.about: Off the patch track and an unreadable running version: the version is judged first.

cases.name: order-an-unreadable-running-version-before-the-minimum
cases.about: Below the minimum and an unreadable running version: the version is judged first, and the running version is not guessed to be 0.0.0.

cases.name: order-an-unreadable-running-version-before-the-service-definition
cases.about: An outdated service definition and an unreadable running version: the version is judged first.
